newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy getting brighter, doubts remain--EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy getting brighter, doubts remain--EPA.

text.p: Latest economic data such as the unemployment rate and industrial production show that Japan's economy is becoming brighter, although uncertainties remain, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Taro Aso told a news conference on Friday.
"Although there are still uncertainties and various problems, the economy is generally moving in a positive direction," Aso said.

He said even though the unemployment rate in January stood at 3.3 percent, unchanged from the previous month, the number of people being forced to leave their jobs had been declining steadily, while those voluntarily quitting to seek new jobs had been increasing. The data was announced earlier on Friday.
He also pointed to strong growth in January industrial output data, announced on Thursday, which showed a rise of 5.3 percent from the previous month.
Aso said one of the problems he was concerned about was deregulation, which was a positive factor but could also work to create unnecessary confusion from changes it brought about.
He also said deregulation was a means for improving people's livelihoods generally, and should not be seen as an end in itself.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto last November announced plans for "Big Bang" deregulation of Japan's financial markets by 2001.
